column1: # Expected divergences between the reference and the port, per stage oracle.
# A structure listed here is allowed to differ; EVERY OTHER structure must match
# exactly. This file is the whole point of the arrangement: a deliberate
# divergence has to be named, justified and bounded, and it cannot quietly grow
# to cover a second structure because someone could not make the second one
# match.
# `equivalence.sh stage index` reports three classes and they are all printed:
#     match      identical to the reference
#     DIVERGED   differs, and is listed here -> expected
#     FAIL       differs, and is NOT listed here -> a bug
# plus the inverse check:
#     STALE      listed here but actually identical -> the divergence is gone,
#                remove the row (otherwise the list rots into a mute list)
# columns:  stage  structure  finding  corpora  notes
#   corpora: a comma-separated list, or "*" for all. Naming corpora matters:
#            on SIRV the Finding 22 divergence is expected to be EMPTY, because
#            every SIRV part has exactly one active gene.
stage
index
column5: the port fills every active gene; the reference uses a leaked loop variable. On SIRV this must still MATCH - 22 of 22 sites there have a single active gene - so SIRV is the control and droso is the test.

column1: align
column5: the port writes QUAL in the same orientation as SEQ; the reference leaves it in the aligned orientation for reverse-strand reads that minimap2 mapped, so its QUAL is reversed relative to its own SEQ. Measured: 759 of 10 000 records on sirv-10k through the minimap2 path (0 with --disable_mm2, where no reorientation happens). Of those, 746 are an exact reversal and 13 are scrambled around a polyA trim site because remove_read_polyA_ends is handed a mismatched seq/qual pair. Affects only the QUAL column.

column1: align
column5: unaligned records (FLAG 4) only. The reference emits whatever read_seq/read_qual the candidate-chaining loop last left behind, so SEQ is the forward or the reverse-complemented read depending on which strand was examined last; the port always writes the read as input. Measured: 2 of 10 000 on sirv-10k, ref SEQ == revcomp(port SEQ) and ref QUAL == reversed(port QUAL) on both.

column1: align
column5: FSM records whose predicted splices match more than one transcript. classify_alignment2.py:27 joins a set of transcript id STRINGS, so the order is PYTHONHASHSEED-dependent and the reference is not self-consistent across runs; the port sorts. Measured: 4 of 10 000 on sirv-10k. Affects only the order within the XA:Z: field, never its contents.

column1: align
column5: reads minimap2 produced no record for (flag 4) reach neither indexed.sam nor unindexed.sam, so the reference's merge has no slot for them and drops uLTRA's alignment; the port keeps it. This is the only approved divergence that changes the NUMBER of records in reads.sam, and the port prints the count on stdout every run. Measured: 4 of 10 000 on sirv-10k (3 of which uLTRA aligned and minimap2 could not) and 1 690 of 20 000 (8.5%) on droso-20k. SIRV understates this badly; droso is the corpus that shows its size.

column1: align
column5: the reference writes '>' headers over four-line bodies and the literal text 'None' when the input has no qualities, which is neither valid FASTA nor valid FASTQ; readfq then mis-parses it and silently loses reads (2 of 4 on the FASTA smoke corpus). The port writes FASTQ when there are qualities and FASTA when there are not. FASTQ input parses correctly either way, so this changes reads.sam only for FASTA input.
